description: AgniSentinel is an AI-powered web dashboard for the Flame in Freefall challenge, predicting fire risks in ISS microgravity. Built with React and FastAPI, it analyzes NASA combustion data (FLEX, ACME, BASS) using Python deep learning to forecast flame behavior. A Gemini API-driven Agentic AI provides autonomous, real-time safety protocols, while Three.js renders interactive 3D flame visuals.
summary:
AgniSentinel is a microgravity fire safety intelligence platform 
built for the NASA Space Apps 2026 "Flame in Freefall" challenge. 
It uses verified NASA Physical Sciences Informatics (PSI) flight 
data from SAFFIRE-I/II/III, BASS-II, SAME/SAME-R, FLEX, and ACME 
experiments to reveal why ground-based NASA-STD-6001 Test #1 
(1g upward-burn) fails to bound low-speed 0–40 cm/s microgravity 
HVAC flows aboard the ISS. The platform features an Interactive 
3D Dual-Gravity Combustion Twin (1g vs 0g), a Lognormal Smoke 
Aerosol Studio grounded in PSI-101 TEM flight data, a 
15-record PSI Flammability Ranker with DOI-linked citations, 
and an AI Investigation Comparator with scope guardrails that 
explicitly excludes rocket propellants. All visualizations are 
grounded in real NASA PSI DOIs — no fabricated data.
details:
AgniSentinel was built using React, Three.js (WebGL GLSL shaders),

Tailwind CSS, and Recharts. The app has 4 integrated workspaces:

1. 3D Dual-Gravity Combustion Twin — parametric physics-guided

visual comparing 1g buoyant cone flames vs 0g spherical flames,

with live controls for ventilation speed (0–40 cm/s), O2%,

fuel geometry, and suppression agent.

2. PSI Flammability Ranker & NASA-STD-6001 Blind-Spot Analyzer —

15 verified PSI records with DOI links, showing where 1g

upward-burn screening tests miss microgravity hazards.

3. Microgravity Smoke Aerosol & Detector Studio — lognormal

particle size distributions from PSI-101 SAME-R TEM data,

showing why ISS smoke detectors can miss 0g pyrolysis events.

4. Investigation Comparator & Mission Co-Pilot — side-by-side

PSI study comparison with AI query assistant and enforced

rocket propellant scope guardrail.

AI coding assistance: Cursor (Claude-based) used during development.

Scientific data: 100% from verified NASA PSI portal and AWS Open Data.
